entities.name: Ulpius Marcellus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ulpius Marcellus was a Roman senator and general of the later second century CE, remembered chiefly as consular governor of Britannia who was later sent back to the province as a field commander under Commodus. Cassius Dio and the Historia Augusta place him among the officers who restored Roman control after serious northern unrest, including warfare along the frontier associated with the Caledonian peoples beyond Hadrian's Wall.

His career illustrates the Antonine–Commodan pattern of recycling experienced consulars into crisis theatres: Britain required both civil administration and hard campaigning, and Marcellus combined the prestige of prior governorship with a reputation for severity. Later anecdote stresses Commodus's suspicion of successful generals, framing Marcellus as a capable but endangered servant of an insecure court.

Whether every dramatic detail is reliable, Ulpius Marcellus stands as a concrete link between provincial governance and frontier war in Roman Britain at the end of the Antonine age, when the northern limes again demanded mobile armies rather than static policing alone.
